headline: How to Create Facebook and Instagram Ads for a Local Gym Promotion With AI
metaDescription: Write an offer brief, generate ad image and headline variants with AdCreative.ai, refine them in Canva and test them in Meta Ads Manager for a local gym promotion.
lede: You have an offer — a free trial week, a seasonal discount — and want it in front of people who live nearby. This guide shows how to turn it into a set of Facebook and Instagram ads with AI, then test which one works.
intro: Paid social is one way for a gym or studio to reach people who live close enough to become members. The slow part is rarely the budget; it's producing enough decent ad variations to learn what works, without a designer or a copywriter.

AI ad tools close that gap. You describe the offer and the audience, and the tool produces a set of image and headline variants sized for each placement. A design tool brings them in line with your brand, and Meta Ads Manager runs them side by side, so results rather than guesswork decide which ad stays.
The workflow below keeps you in charge of the parts AI can't do — the offer, the local detail and the final check — and lets it handle the volume.
learningOutcomes: How to write an offer brief an AI ad tool can work from
How to generate several ad image and headline variants from one brief
How to bring AI-generated creative in line with your brand in Canva
How to launch a small test in Meta Ads Manager and keep the ad that performs

beforeYouStart.title: One clear offer
beforeYouStart.description: A single promotion with a deadline, such as a free trial week or a seasonal membership discount.

beforeYouStart.title: Your brand assets
beforeYouStart.description: Logo, brand colours and a few real photos of your space, classes or team.

beforeYouStart.title: A Facebook Page and Meta Ads Manager
beforeYouStart.description: Launching the ads still needs basic familiarity with Ads Manager.

beforeYouStart.title: Accounts on the tools
beforeYouStart.description: AdCreative.ai and Canva each need a sign-up. Check current plans on their sites before you commit.

beforeYouStart.title: A test budget
beforeYouStart.description: A small daily amount you're comfortable spending while the variants run against each other.

steps.title: Write the offer brief
steps.body: Put the offer, the audience, the area and the call to action into a few lines the AI can work from.
explanation: Every ad tool works from what you give it. A vague brief ("promote the gym") produces vague ads; a specific one ("free trial week, people within five miles, book a free class") produces ads someone can act on.
Writing the brief first also keeps every variant honest: the same offer, the same terms and the same deadline in every ad.
instructions: Write the offer in one line, including any deadline or conditions.
Describe who it's for and where — the area around your location.
Choose one call to action, such as "Book your free class".
Note anything that must not change: prices, dates, terms.
steps.expectedOutcome: A short brief covering the offer, audience, area, call to action and fixed terms.
tips: One offer per campaign. Two offers in one ad make both harder to read.

steps.title: Generate ad variants
steps.body: Give the brief to an AI ad generator and get several image and headline variations sized for Facebook and Instagram.
explanation: Testing needs options. An AI ad generator turns one brief into a set of images and headlines sized for each placement, so you're choosing between variants rather than starting from a blank canvas.
Treat the output as a first draft. Some variants will miss your brand or your audience — you're looking for three or four worth refining.
instructions: Open AdCreative.ai and start a new set of creatives.
Paste the prompt below, adjusted to your offer and area.
Add your logo and brand colours if the tool asks for them.
Shortlist three or four variants that are clear, on-brand and accurate.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.why: It produces sets of ad images and headline variations sized for each platform from one brief — built for making many variants to test rather than one hero ad.

steps.prompt: Create 3 Facebook/Instagram ad variations promoting a free trial week at our gym, targeting people within 5 miles, with a clear 'Book your free class' call to action.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three or four shortlisted variants, each with an image and a headline.
tips: Check every price, date and claim in the generated copy against your brief — generated text can drift from the offer.

steps.title: Refine the creative in Canva
steps.body: Bring the shortlisted ads in line with your brand, swap in real photos, and resize them for each placement.
explanation: Generated ads often look generic. Replacing stock-style imagery with real photos of your space and team makes an ad look like your gym rather than any gym — and it's what people will see when they walk in.
This is also where you check sizes. Feed and stories placements use different shapes, and a design cropped badly in one of them wastes that placement.
instructions: Upload the shortlisted variants to Canva.
Swap generated imagery for your own photos where it helps.
Apply your brand fonts and colours, and keep the text on the image short.
Resize each design for feed and stories placements, then export.

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Template-driven design with photo editing and resizing for different channels, so each ad fits its placement and matches your brand.

steps.expectedOutcome: On-brand ad images in the sizes each placement needs.

steps.title: Finish the ad copy
steps.body: Pair each image with a headline and a short primary text that state the offer plainly.
explanation: The image stops the scroll; the text makes the offer. Keep it plain: what it is, who it's for, when it ends, and what to do next.
Generated headlines are a starting point. Keep the ones that sound like the way you talk to members, and cut anything that promises more than the offer does.
instructions: Take the headline variants from step 2, or generate more from the same brief.
Write one short primary text per ad: the offer, the area, the deadline and the call to action.
Remove anything your front desk couldn't back up.
Match each final headline to an image.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.why: Its headline variants give you options to choose from and edit, rather than a single line to accept.

steps.expectedOutcome: Every ad has an image, a headline and primary text that state the offer accurately.

steps.title: Launch a test in Meta Ads Manager
steps.body: Set up one campaign with your variants, target the local area, and let the results show which ad to keep.
explanation: Running several variants at once is the point of the whole workflow: the audience shows you which image and headline work, and you stop paying for the ones that don't.
Keep the test simple — one offer, one area, the same budget behind each variant — so a difference in results actually means something.
instructions: In Meta Ads Manager, create a campaign for the promotion.
Target the area around your location and the audience from your brief.
Add each variant as its own ad within the same ad set.
After a few days, pause the weakest ads and keep the strongest running.

tools.name: Meta Ads Manager
tools.why: Where the ads actually run. Launching them needs some familiarity with it.

steps.expectedOutcome: A live campaign running your variants against each other, with results you can compare.
tips: Change one thing at a time in the next test, so you know what made the difference.

expectedResult.summary: A local Facebook and Instagram campaign for your promotion, with three or four on-brand ad variants running against each other — and results that show which one to keep.
checklist: Every ad states the same offer, terms and deadline
Real photos of your gym replace generic imagery where possible
Nothing in the copy promises more than the offer does
The campaign targets the area around your location
You've decided when you'll review the results

tips: Photograph your space, classes and team once in good light, and reuse the set across campaigns.
Keep a short log of each test — offer, variants, results — so the next campaign starts from what you learned.
Send the click where the ad promises: if it says "Book your free class", it should land on booking.
Plan promotions ahead so the creative isn't rushed in the week the offer starts.

commonIssues.solution: Give the tool your logo and brand colours, make the brief more specific, and swap in real photos in Canva.

commonIssues.problem: An ad gets a detail of the offer wrong
commonIssues.solution: Check every price, date and condition against your brief before launch and correct the copy. Don't rely on the generator to keep terms exact.

commonIssues.problem: A design is cropped badly in stories
commonIssues.solution: Resize the design for that placement in Canva rather than letting one size cover every placement.

commonIssues.problem: You'd rather not learn Ads Manager
commonIssues.solution: Launching these ads needs basic familiarity with it. If you'd rather hand that part off, see the related guide on running local Facebook ads without learning Ads Manager.

closing.title: Turn your next promotion into ads that are tested, not guessed
closing.body: Start with step 1 — a clear offer brief takes a few minutes and shapes every ad that follows. After the first test, you'll have a workflow you can reuse for every promotion.
